# Waitloop

> Developer-native waiting layer for coding agents. Hooks report minimal lifecycle state; games fill short waits; work takes priority again when the agent needs attention.

Canonical agent integration guide: https://waitloop.run/agent.md
Guide mirror (raw GitHub): https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shixushi2025/waitloop/main/apps/web/public/agent.md
Guide mirror (GitHub UI): https://github.com/shixushi2025/waitloop/blob/main/apps/web/public/agent.md
Machine-readable manifest: https://waitloop.run/agent.json
Waitloop skill: https://waitloop.run/skills/waitloop/SKILL.md
Room API: https://waitloop.run/api/v1/rooms
Room-specific join pattern: https://waitloop.run/join/<join-code>
Game MCP endpoint: https://waitloop.run/mcp
CLI alpha install/update: npm install -g @waitloop/cli@alpha
CLI diagnostics: waitloop doctor
Health: https://waitloop.run/api/v1/health
Source: https://github.com/shixushi2025/waitloop

If an Agent browser blocks direct navigation to agent.md, use a declared mirror or agent.json instead of assuming Waitloop/Cloudflare is down.

Seat and Actor are separate. New Dou Dizhu rooms use stable room-scoped Seat IDs. Actor ID is not a credential. Controllers play; Advisors may inspect/comment on the one Seat they are explicitly bound to.

Web is optional. A headless Agent can `POST /api/v1/rooms` with mode `agent-bots`, claim the returned Join code, then use MCP.

`waitloop join <code>` claims and caches a temporary room Actor credential. Join success is not MCP connection: an authenticated request must reach `/mcp` before the Actor is online. The CLI does not hot-inject a newly claimed MCP server into an already-running harness session.

Current MCP tools: get_turn(), play_move(expectedRevision, moveId), comment(text), yield_to_bot(), take_control().

MCP does not wake an Agent after the Agent returns a final response. If the user asks to keep playing or play until finished, keep the current Agent run active until that stopping condition. Current alpha has no wait_for_turn(), so avoid tight polling when another Human/connected Actor owns the turn.

`yield_to_bot()` temporarily delegates an owned Seat to a deterministic Bot without changing Seat/hand/role/history. The cached room credential can reconnect; `take_control()` explicitly restores the owner. Casual fallback is never triggered solely by elapsed time.

Join codes are one-time and short-lived; rooms also expire. Human browser sessions use a persistent anonymous Actor ID plus a separate HttpOnly credential to recover room access without requiring an account.

Codex command hooks require Codex review/trust even when bundled by a Plugin. A Plugin may improve packaging but does not remove the hook trust step.

Lifecycle hooks and game MCP remain separate security scopes.
